The core platform's `getGlobalProperty` is called from the REST module `openmrs-module-webservices.rest`, which holds the `/ws/rest/v1` code. `openmrs-core` has no `webservices/rest` tree. The most exposed caller is `RequestContext`, which reads the default and absolute result limits on every request that goes through it.

**Generic `/ws/rest/v1` request path (most likely affected)**
- `RequestContext` reads `RestUtil.getDefaultLimit()` into its default `limit` field and checks against `RestUtil.getAbsoluteLimit()`, which throws if the limit is exceeded (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod-common/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/RequestContext.java:36`, `:140-141`).
- `RestUtil.getGlobalProperty(name, default)` is the private wrapper that every RestUtil lookup goes through (`openmrs-module-webservices.rest/omod-common/src/main/java/org/openmrs/module/webservices/rest/web/RestUtil.java:71-79`).
- `RestUtil.getDefaultLimit()` and `getAbsoluteLimit()` parse the limit properties (`RestUtil.java:87-101`, `:109-122`).
- `RestUtil.getAllowedIps()` feeds the IP allow-list check (`RestUtil.java:222-234`). Its caller at line 134 is also in scope.
- `RestUtil.setUriPrefix()` sets the URI prefix at startup and on context refresh, and is called from `RestConstants.java:85` and `RestUtil.java:683`, `:691`.
- The error-response builder reads the stack-trace-details flag (`RestUtil.java:836-851`).
